modules.title: HTTP and REST APIs
modules.description: Understand web communication and API design

steps.content: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is the foundation of web communication. Client (browser, app) sends a request to a server, which responds. Request: method (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE), URL, headers, optional body. Response: status code, headers, body.

Common methods: GET (retrieve), POST (create), PUT/PATCH (update), DELETE (remove). Status codes: 2xx success (200 OK, 201 Created), 3xx redirect (301, 302), 4xx client error (400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found), 5xx server error (500 Internal Server Error).

steps.question: Which HTTP method is used to retrieve a resource?
steps.explanation: GET requests data from a server. It should be safe (no side effects) and idempotent (multiple calls = same result).

steps.question: The status code for 'Not Found' is ______.
steps.explanation: 404 means the requested resource doesn't exist on the server.

steps.question: Order the parts of an HTTP request
steps.explanation: Request line -> headers -> blank line -> optional body. GET requests typically have no body.

steps.question: POST requests should be idempotent.
steps.explanation: POST is NOT idempotent - multiple identical POST requests create multiple resources. PUT and DELETE are idempotent.

steps.question: What does a 201 Created status code mean?
options: Request succeeded and resource was created
steps.explanation: 201 is the standard success code for POST requests that create a new resource. Response often includes Location header with new resource URL.

steps.content: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style for APIs. Resources are nouns (users, posts), not verbs. URLs represent resources: GET /users (list), GET /users/123 (single), POST /users (create), PUT /users/123 (update), DELETE /users/123 (delete).

Use plural nouns for collections (/users not /user). Version APIs in URL (/api/v1/users). Use HTTP status codes correctly. Return JSON. Filter/sort/paginate with query params: GET /users?page=2&limit=20&sort=name. Nested resources: /users/123/posts.

steps.question: Which URL follows REST conventions for getting a specific user?
steps.explanation: REST uses nouns (plural) and HTTP methods. GET /users/123 retrieves user 123. No verbs in URL.

steps.question: To create a new user, send a ______ request to /users.
steps.explanation: POST to collection URL creates a new resource. The server assigns the ID.

steps.question: Order these REST endpoints for a posts resource
steps.explanation: Standard CRUD mapping: list, create, read, update, delete.

steps.question: PUT replaces the entire resource; PATCH partially updates it.
steps.explanation: PUT expects full resource representation (replaces). PATCH applies partial updates. Both are idempotent.

steps.question: How do you filter results in a REST API?
steps.explanation: Query parameters for filtering, sorting, pagination: GET /users?active=true&role=admin. Keeps URL clean.

steps.content: API authentication: API keys (simple, in header/query), Bearer tokens (JWT in Authorization header), OAuth 2.0 (delegated access), Session cookies (traditional web). Always use HTTPS. Never put secrets in URLs.

Authorization: after authentication, check permissions. RBAC (Role-Based Access Control): user has role, role has permissions. ABAC (Attribute-Based): policies based on attributes. Rate limiting prevents abuse. CORS controls cross-origin requests. Validate and sanitize all input.

steps.question: Where should a JWT be sent in an HTTP request?
options: In the URL as a query parameter
In the Authorization header as Bearer token
steps.explanation: Standard: Authorization: Bearer <token>. Keeps token out of URLs (logs) and separates from body.

steps.question: The HTTP header for cross-origin resource sharing is ______.
steps.explanation: CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin, etc.) control which origins can access your API. Set by server.

steps.question: Order to make an authenticated API request with fetch
steps.explanation: Include Authorization header with Bearer token in fetch options.

steps.question: Rate limiting should only apply to authenticated endpoints.
steps.explanation: Rate limit ALL endpoints (including auth/login) to prevent brute force and DoS. Different limits for different endpoint types.

steps.question: What is the purpose of a refresh token in OAuth 2.0?
options: To refresh the access token when it expires
steps.explanation: Access tokens are short-lived. Refresh tokens are long-lived and used to obtain new access tokens without re-authentication.

steps.content: JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is the standard API data format. Request: Content-Type: application/json header. Body: JSON.stringify(data). Response: check ok status, parse with response.json(). Handle errors: network errors, HTTP errors, validation errors.

Error responses should be consistent: { error: { code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: 'Invalid input', details: [...] } }. Client-side: try/catch for network, check response.ok for HTTP errors, parse error body for details. Retry with exponential backoff for 5xx/429.

steps.question: What Content-Type header should you send with JSON data?
steps.explanation: application/json tells the server the body contains JSON. Server uses this to parse correctly.

steps.question: To parse a JSON response in JavaScript, use response.______().
steps.explanation: response.json() parses the response body as JSON and returns a promise resolving to the parsed object.

steps.question: Order to POST JSON data and handle response
steps.explanation: Fetch with POST, JSON headers, stringified body. Check ok, then parse JSON.

steps.question: A 422 Unprocessable Entity status means the server understood the request but validation failed.
steps.explanation: 422 is used for semantic errors - request is well-formed but fails business logic/validation. Different from 400 (malformed request).

steps.question: What should you do on a 500 Internal Server Error?
steps.explanation: 5xx errors are server-side. Retry with exponential backoff (wait longer between retries). Don't retry immediately - adds load.
